background: Helaba is the Landesbank of Hesse and Thuringia, owned by the regional savings banks and the two states, a wholesale and real-estate lender that also acts as the central bank for its savings banks and owns the Frankfurter Sparkasse.
synthesis: Two of the three main agencies rate the bank, at AA- on average and both on a stable outlook, with the last move a one-notch upgrade by one of the three on 12 May 2026, grades resting on the savings-bank sector's protection scheme and state ownership. Capital is on the weak side of EU and Nordic peers, with CET1 of 15.8% and leverage of 5.4% both a little below the peer medians, and CET1 down 0.5 points since 30 Jun 2025. Liquidity is mixed, with LCR of 168% above the median and NSFR of 120% below it. The flagged news is the concern: commercial real-estate losses in the first half reported on 31 Aug 2026, after an earlier write-down on an office sale and a BaFin order to fix money-laundering controls.
